function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

That seems odd. It says data_points: "price" | "volume"[]. That means data_points can be either the string "price" or an array of strings "volume"? Actually the type is ambiguous. But likely they want to pass an array of data points like ["price", "volume"]. But the type says "price" | "volume"[], which might mean either "price" or an array of "volume". That seems wrong. But we can guess that we need to pass an array of data points: ["price", "volume"].

We need to call the function for each symbol. The symbols: Apple Inc. is AAPL. Alphabet (Google) is GOOGL or GOOG. Microsoft is MSFT. They are all listed on NASDAQ, not NYSE. But the user says "紐約證券交易所" (NYSE). Apple, Google, Microsoft are on NASDAQ. But maybe they want the data anyway. We'll just provide the data. Use the function get_stock_data for each symbol with data_points ["price", "volume"].
